rationale.conceptual: The PHQ method involves computing mode‑projected VAFs, fitting renormalized frequencies, Fourier interpolation to thermodynamic limit, and integrating entropy to get free energy. This requires deep understanding of phonon physics, DFT, and statistical mechanics. Several interacting components (harmonic phonon, AIMD, VAF fitting, EOS fitting, Gibbs free energy) must be correctly implemented.
rationale.execution: The pipeline requires running DFT static and phonon calculations, multiple AIMD simulations across a range of volumes and temperatures, then extensive post‑processing (VAF computation, fitting, interpolation, entropy integration, free energy fitting, EOS, property derivation, and phase boundary determination). Orchestrating these steps with correct file management and ensuring consistency across many parameters is highly non‑trivial and prone to failure.
